title: MDM for Startups: When You Need It and What to Look For
summary: Does your startup need MDM? When to adopt mobile device management, why customers ask about it in security reviews, what to look for, and what it costs.
body_markdown:
Question to ask


How Oneleet MDM answers


Does it enforce the device settings my compliance program requires and my customers expect?


**Compliant by default.** Oneleet MDM is synced with your compliance program, so your framework’s device requirements become enforced settings. That includes the encryption, screen lock and firewall questions that come up in customer security reviews. Secure defaults set the baseline in one click, and you can see and adjust every setting per device.


When my compliance tool flags a device, can I fix it in the same place?


**Fix it where you see it.** With a separate MDM, a failing check in your compliance tool sends you to another vendor’s console to fix it. Most compliance tools read your MDM, whereas Oneleet runs it. An admin updates the policy in the same platform that flagged the problem, and it applies to every managed laptop without asking employees to change anything.


Are the device checks tied to my security program’s requirements, in a format my auditor can use?


**Proof your auditor can use.** Collecting evidence automatically doesn’t help if it’s evidence of the wrong state. Oneleet’s device checks are tied to your security program’s requirements, and because the settings are enforced, the evidence shows devices that are actually secure. Device data goes straight to your auditor, with an activity log for each device.


Does it add a second vendor, console, and contract?


**One vendor.** MDM and compliance come on one platform and one contract, charged per managed device per month. There’s no second console to check and no integration to maintain.
